T: Pull the sword. Then do the dishes.
D: A young boy called Wart is tutored by the wizard Merlin and pulls the sword from the stone.
P: Serve the mains when Merlin magics the castle dishes into washing themselves.
S: Thick slices of crusty bread with aged cheddar, pickled onions and apple wedges on a big wooden board.
Walnuts, hazelnuts and almonds tossed with honey and cinnamon, roasted at 170C for 15 minutes, cooled into clusters.
Wart turned into a fish in the castle moat
Flathead pieces dusted in seasoned flour, fried in hot oil until crisp, served with tartare sauce and lemon wedges.
M: Wart working in the castle kitchen
Pork shoulder roasted at 160C for 4 hours with crackling, with roast potatoes, apples and gravy.
the New Year's tournament in London
Beef and ale pie simmered 3 hours, under a puff pastry lid baked at 200C, with mash and peas.
W: Suet-style pastry spread with raspberry jam, rolled, baked at 180C for 40 minutes, sliced with hot custard.
K: Merlin's sugar bowl that walks itself to the cup
English breakfast tea with milk and sugar cubes.

s.how: Tear a loaf of crusty bread into thick chunks and pile onto a big wooden board. Add wedges of aged cheddar, a bowl of pickled onions and green apple wedges. Set it in the middle of the table like a lord's supper in a draughty castle hall.

Toss 100g each of walnuts, hazelnuts and almonds with 3 tbsp honey and a pinch of cinnamon. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 15 minutes, stirring once. Cool completely so they set, then break into clusters for little paws.

m.note: the New Year's tournament in London
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck with 2 sliced onions. Add 375ml brown ale and water to cover and simmer for 3 hours. Thicken, spoon into a dish and top with puff pastry. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with buttery mash and peas.

w.how: Rub 100g butter into 300g self-raising flour, then add enough milk to make a soft dough. Roll into a rectangle, spread with raspberry jam and roll up. Wrap loosely in baking paper and bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Slice and pour over hot custard.

d.note: Merlin's sugar bowl that walks itself to the cup
d.how: Warm a teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 4 tea bags and a litre of freshly boiled water and steep for 4 minutes. Pour into cups and serve with milk and a bowl of sugar cubes. A sugar bowl that walks on its own is optional.
